hypothesis: Exhaustive physical parent/edge coverage, linked multi-goal distance and candidate supervision, and fixed replay can extend finite learned maps to untrained relations between seen states.

initialization.optimizer: fresh Adam; retain learned weights only

continuation.optimizer: restore weights and Adam from the completed two-epoch run
continuation.sampler: restore exact RNG and exposure; deterministically reconstruct legacy checkpoints without sampler state

supervision: Each shuffled parent occurs once per epoch. Supervise all six physical edges at exact distance one. Each star faces its own distance-stratified goal and another star's goal; calibrate all seven star-to-goal distances and rank every six-way decision. Replay cycles through eight fixed old pools (complete within-pool distances and candidate labels), then one fixed global relation cohort (all parent/candidate-to-goal labels). No coordinate answers or additional learned readout.
split: All physical states may train. Hold out unordered parent/goal and all six successor/goal relations for validation, test and historical cohorts, from every absolute and ranking label. Targets have distance >=4, so withholding them does not conflict with exhaustive action-edge supervision. Replay is verified disjoint. A task is an unseen initial relation; its full rollout can enter other trained relations. This replaces the historical protected-state protocol and is not an unseen-state test.
selection: Continue the existing two epochs to 100 total complete state passes, preserving Adam and sampling position. Primary final checkpoint; no heldout selection or early stopping. Save epoch checkpoints. No automatic extension beyond 100 or alternative architecture.
acceptance: Report exact parent and directed edge coverage; train and heldout distance errors by distance, shortest-action rate, unrestricted full greedy arrival and cycles; fixed old-map retention. State-seen interpretation requires all cohort inputs encountered as training parents. No whole-space zero-error claim; finite budget failure does not prove supervision can never suffice.
